prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"claims": [{"claim": 1, "text": "Continuous enzymatic saccharification in membrane bioreactors with 10 kDa ultrafiltration modules can maintain acceptable flux through daily 15 min backwash protocols, with enzyme retention of 87–92% sustained over 14 days of continuous operation.", "sources": [{"id": "SYN-PUB-03519", "field": "abstract", "quote": "10 kDa cutoff hollow-fibre ultrafiltration module was evaluated for continuous enzymatic saccharification with enzyme recycle"}]}, {"claim": 2, "text": "Polyethersulfone ultrafiltration membranes fouled with biomass-rich streams can recover to 93.1% or 97.4% of original water flux using alkaline cleaning protocols, though higher flux recovery protocols may reduce membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cleaning cycles.", "sources": [{"id": "SYN-PUB-03378", "field": "abstract", "quote": "Protocol B achieved the highest PWFR of 97.4% for polyethersulphone membranes but reduced membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cleaning cycles"}]}, {"claim": 3, "text": "High-solids enzymatic hydrolysis requires consideration of slurry rheology, and enzyme recycling via ultrafiltration membrane recycle presents techno-economic implications for bioprocess scale-up.", "sources": [{"id": "SYN-PUB-03514", "field": "abstract", "quote": "ultrafiltration membrane recycle and magnetic particle immobilisation — and their techno-economic implications"}]}]}
